abstract: Pathway enrichment helps interpret the many genes targeted by microRNAs (miRNAs), but comparisons across organisms are complicated by differences in target evidence and functional annotation. Here, we present miRPathDB 2027, which extends miRPathDB from human and mouse to rat and rhesus macaque. Its retained enrichment profiles span 5701 miRNA entries and 28 044 pathway and ontology accessions from Gene Ontology, Reactome, and WikiPathways. Three cumulative evidence tiers allow users to examine how associations change as broader experimental records and computational predictions are included. Cross-species views align curated miRNA families, separated by mature arm, with corresponding pathway terms and indicate unavailable comparisons; a prespecified analysis tests whether orthologous miRNA profiles agree more than expected from matched random target sets. Interactive miRNA and pathway profiles, heat maps, versioned downloads, and programmatic access connect these patterns to the underlying targets and evidence. miRPathDB 2027 supports exploration of miRNA function and prioritization of associations for experimental follow-up. The database web interface is freely available without registration at https://web.ccb.uni-saarland.de/mirpathdb/.
